title:
Double Advanced
Math Program
body:
Ten weeks of weekend math
Models, reasoning, and daily practice
text:
Double Advanced
Math Program
Ten weeks of models, reasoning, and practice.
Make the math visible.

notes.say: We will make sense of the math together.
notes.ask: What would you like to understand better?
notes.expect: A personal goal or question.
notes.if_stuck: Invite a drawing or an example.

visual_description: A fraction area model provides the mathematical cover image.

title: How a session runs
body:
Recall earlier math.
Try a problem before seeing a method.
Use a model, then compare ideas.
Explain the idea in your own words.
Finish with one independent problem.
text:
How a session runs
Recall
Bring back earlier math.
Try
Start before seeing a method.
Represent
Use objects or a drawing.
Discuss
Compare two approaches.
Explain
Put the idea into words.
Check
Solve one on your own.

notes.say: The first attempt helps us decide what to discuss.
notes.ask: Which part gives you time to explain?
notes.expect: Compare ideas and summarize.
notes.if_stuck: Point to the sequence and name each stage.

title: The twenty sessions
text: The twenty sessions

notes.say: Each week builds on earlier ideas.
notes.ask: Which topic connects to something you know?
notes.expect: One named connection.
notes.if_stuck: Point to fractions and ratios. These return often.

text:
Fractions on one number line
I can compare fractions and decimals by placing them on the same number line.

title: Same denominator
text:
Same denominator
Compare {3/7} and {5/7}. Write <, >, or =.

notes.say: Read P1. Give time to try before comparing methods.
notes.ask: Are both fractions using the same whole? Which point lies farther right?
notes.expect: P1: {3/7} < {5/7}. Both use sevenths. Three parts are fewer than five.
notes.if_stuck: Draw equal-sized wholes. Mark a benchmark or rename both fractions in equal-sized parts.

visual_description: Problem and model side by side with numberline scaffolding. Answers are withheld.

title: Same numerator
text:
Same numerator
Compare {4/5} and {4/9}. Use strips of the same length.
Is {5/12} less than or greater than {1/2}?

notes.say: Read P2 and P3. Give time to try before comparing methods.
notes.ask: Are both fractions using the same whole? Which point lies farther right?
notes.expect: P2: {4/5} > {4/9}. Fifths are larger than ninths, so four fifths cover more. P3: Less than {1/2}. Half of twelve parts is six parts. Five twelfths is below half.
notes.if_stuck: Draw equal-sized wholes. Mark a benchmark or rename both fractions in equal-sized parts.

title: Fraction versus decimal
text:
Fraction versus decimal
Compare {7/10} and 0.68.
A line has ticks at 0, 2, and 4. Place 2 {1/2}.

notes.say: Read P6 and P7. Give time to try before comparing methods.
notes.ask: Are both fractions using the same whole? Which point lies farther right?
notes.expect: P6: {7/10} > 0.68. {7/10} = 0.70, which is 2 hundredths more than 0.68. P7: One fourth of the way from 2 to 4. The interval from 2 to 4 is two units. Half a unit uses one fourth of that interval.
notes.if_stuck: Draw equal-sized wholes. Mark a benchmark or rename both fractions in equal-sized parts.

Three meters of ribbon are cut into {1/4}-meter pieces. How many pieces?

notes.say: Read P5 and P6. Give time to try before comparing methods.
notes.ask: What is the group size? Are we finding how many groups or how much per group?

title: Words and meaning
text:
Words and meaning
Scaling
Multiplying an amount to change its size.
{1/2} × 8 takes half of eight.
Unit fraction
A fraction with numerator 1.
{1/5} is one fifth.
Product
The result of multiplication.
{1/2} × 8 has product 4.

notes.say: Use each word while pointing to a model.
notes.ask: Which example shows the meaning most clearly?
notes.expect: {1/2} × 8 takes half of eight. {1/5} is one fifth. {1/2} × 8 has product 4.

coordinate pair
Two numbers naming horizontal and vertical position.
(−2, 3) means left 2, up 3.
reflection
A mirror image across a line.

inequality
A comparison using <, >, ≤, or ≥.
h ≥ 10 includes 10 and larger numbers.
